t: Engine anchors
x: The facts nearly every task needs. Details: kb/engine-anchors.md , kb/binary-code.md , kb/factionmember.md , kb/gamedb-schema.md . - Image vs heap. ShadowOfWar.exe always loads at 0x140000000 (RELOCS STRIPPED, no DYNAMIC BASE): image and static addresses are fixed, absolute = base + RVA . The HEAP moves every launch: never cache a heap address across sessions; stamp evidence with pid / base / session. - Code lives in two sections. .arch (0x1000-0x1D87C00) and executable .bss a (0x2C89000-0x729714D, the protector's region, reached only through vtables, so callers of == 0 there proves nothing). .text is a 20-byte decoy; vtables live in .xtext . Take executability from the section table. .pdata is not the function universe (leaves have no entry, 26,293 entries are fragments): the function list is the xref index's. - Managers. GameManager [base+0x26FFAA8] . FactionSystem FS = [GM+0x6C68] : pools FS+0x68 (0xC0 each, members +0x18/+0x20; the MainGame pool holds every captain), army contexts FS+0x98 (38 x 0x290, ctx = entry+8), current region FS+0x1B0 (record name), its faction FS+0x1B8 . Six "managers" are fake and must never be used: AIManager 0x2A34D00, PlayerManager 0x2A34BE0, ArmyMan

t: Laws
x: One line each; full text and history in kb/hard-won-rules.md and the topic file named. - Never write FM / SMC / inventory / GameDB while loading: the deserialiser is rebuilding them (crash 2026-07-06). - Never memcpy-clone an entity or inject into SpawnManager; create objects through the engine's factory ( kb/live-world-objects.md ). - Never bulk-mutate hot-thread GameDB domains (NativeLife, Camera, Interface/WorldUI, AudioHook RTPCs, Profile, AI/Sensors, Structures ) with int / vec / enum / FK writes. Repoint an enum cell only COLD, guarded on its old value ( kb/army-menu.md camera). - Never write raw bytes at a vec slot or into a shared vec blob from a bulk tool; packed bools are single-bit read-modify-write; never dereference a type-5 cell ( kb/gamedb-schema.md ). - A RecordLink write must match the field's DECLARED type: SetLink only checks it is some record (crash at the shot, 2026-10-07, kb/quests-story-scenes.md savior). - A record with header byte +0x01 bit 0x10 (every BlendDB .bvr record, 0x1A) is a native struct: write instance + SlotOffset , never instance + link 8 ( kb/gamedb-schema.md , 2026-10-27). - Never modify shared GDB records (Smp wrappers, Facial chains). - Nev

t: Combat behaviour measured live (2026-10-28) and the global AI constants
x: Live combat capture (MEASURED, desert, 73.5 s of world clock, 1,215 samples, read-only; combat capture.py in the session scratchpad): up to 17 NPCs engaged against the player, one fight circle (the player's) the whole time. In 122 timeline samples, NPCs whose leaf step was Attack : 0 in 65, 1 in 32, 2 in 25, never 3+. Typical snapshot: 10-12 in CircleTarget , 1-2 in Attack . Leaf transitions: CircleTarget - Attack 30, Attack - CircleTarget 25, GoToPreferredAttackPosition - CircleTarget 25, CircleTarget - CombatRecoil 19, CircleTarget - GoToPreferredAttackPosition 17, CombatRecoil - CircleTarget 16. t: BNDL v6 Format (CORRECTED 2026-08-06 — byte-identical emit 1,276/1,276)
x: .bndl is the manifest for the paired .embb , and it MIRRORS it: same path table, same path offsets, and the same payload-size array the EMBB carries as size prefixes . [0x00] "BNDL" magic [0x04] u32 version (6) [0x08] u32 path table size == the paired EMBB's [0x0C] u32 path table size + align4(len(type string)+1) [0x10] u32 asset count == the paired EMBB's [0x14] asset count × u32 PAYLOAD SIZES ← identical to the EMBB's size prefixes [0x14 + ac 4] path table (path table size bytes) — identical BYTES to the EMBB's [after path table] "Bundles/Types:XXX" null-terminated, then 4-aligned [then] asset count × u32 path offsets — identical to the EMBB's [0x0C] is NOT [0x08] + 28 . That held on 995 of 1,276 sampled manifests and failed on 281 (deltas 20/24/32/36/40). The rule is [0x0C] = path table size + align4(len(bundle type)+1) — i.e. the combined length of the path table plus the type string region — which holds 1,276/1,276 . Emitting the constant 28 produces a corrupt manifest for ~22% of bundles. Bundle types are open-ended, not a fixed three: Presentation (208,575), WorldQuest , Sound 1 , FlairWorld , Flair 1MB , WorldLighting , ThroneRoomBarrows , UI Tutorial , QuestCinBundle , … —

t: SKDB v9 Format (CRACKED 2026-04-23)
x: Serialized Key Database — per-region/per-language string override tables. [0x00] u32 magic "SKDB" [0x04] u32 version (9) [0x08] u32 header size (28) [0x0C] u32 key count (total hash entries across all language sections) [0x10] u32 reserved (0) [0x14] u32 string pool size (byte size of the UTF-16LE string pool at EOF) [0x18] u32 reserved (0) [0x1C] u32 lang count (19) [0x20] lang count × (u32 section data offset, u32 cumulative metric) [after section table] Initial key lookup table: 8-byte entries [at each section data offset] Per-language key lookup tables: 8-byte entries [EOF - string pool size] String pool: flat, null-terminated UTF-16LE strings Each 8-byte key entry: u16 hash lo, u16 hash hi, u16 secondary hash, u16 string index ( string index = 0-based index into the flat string pool). Access via aire.formats.StringEditor .

t: EMBB v5 Format (RE-CRACKED 2026-08-06 — THERE IS NO PADDING)
x: aire/formats/embb.py ; call("embb probe" / "embb verify" / "embb replace") . Offline. Full write-up: aire/documents/EMBB BNDL CONTAINER.md . Byte-identical rebuild from parsed parts 400/400 — the only standard that counts. Population verified COMPLETE (not sampled): 190,407 EMBB blobs, 100% version 5 and 225,311 BNDL blobs, 100% version 6 — no version variants exist. Header + path-table invariants pass on 190,407/190,407 = 100.0000% . [0x00] u32 magic "EMBB" [0x04] u32 version (5) [0x08] u32 path table size [0x0C] u32 asset count [0x10] path table: asset count NUL-terminated ASCII paths, each NUL-padded to a 4-byte boundary. path table size == end of the last aligned path, EXACTLY. [0x10 + pts] asset count × u32 — byte offset of each PATH, relative to 0x10. This is a path index, NOT a section table. [then] asset count × [ u32 payload size ; payload ] payload begins with its own 4-char tag, chosen by the path's EXTENSION. Measured over 964 containers / 35 archives / 8,218 sections (all version 5): invariant result --- --- chain terminates exactly on EOF 964/964 , slack 0 path table size == end of last aligned path 964/964 path offsets 4-aligned and chained by aligned length 964/964

t: Record -> ASSET link (COMPUTED 2026-08-03) — `aire/formats/asset_link.py`
x: The engine graph joined binary/GADB/live but never the record- asset edge; the 400,248-path archive index and the GADB sat as two disconnected worlds. call("asset link build") computes the whole set offline in ~7s: 26,999 edges over 14,632 distinct paths and 19,322 records . All 25 GADB-bearing archives are MERGED in archcfg order, not read one at a time. Reading only hotchunk was incomplete: over the 31,966 String values where hotchunk and Patch 04 LC disagree, hotchunk uniquely resolves 1,809 and the patch uniquely resolves 1,651 — the loser is almost always UNSET (empty, or a string offset below 13 , which reads a suffix of the block's root type name GameDatabase and surfaced as the literal 'ameDatabase' ). Highest-priority non-unset value wins; each edge records its gadb source . Purely additive: 0 edges changed, 0 removed, 1,996 added (e.g. Character/Models::DarkTalion.BehaviorResource - behaviors\player\player elf.bvr ). Values are read at the offset each String/String2 field actually REFERENCES, never by splitting the string block on NUL — the block is shared-SUFFIX, and the split route produced paths with foreign leading bytes ( \x10@fx\characters\... ). Path shape is const

t: The container hop — `aire/formats/bundle_index.py` (CLOSED 2026-08-03)
x: A .bndl is the manifest for its paired .embb and lists the SOURCE paths it holds, so it is the map from "asset the GADB asked for" to "container that ships it". 224,871 .bndl -named entries - 219,031 content-verified manifests (97.4%) , 1.87M membership edges, ~150s. A NAME DOES NOT ADDRESS A BLOB — key membership by (ARCHIVE, ENTRY INDEX). Several entries legitimately share one name offset : Patch 06 LC has 32 groups of 4-5 distinct blobs on a single name string (different offsets, different sizes — variant copies, not chunks and not duplicates), and Patch 01 has 400 such entries. A name is a LABEL; only the entry index is an address. Two earlier attempts failed because they went through names: - keying by bundle path alone — the same path ships in several archives ( ingame navmarkers.bndl exists at two paths), so a global first-wins archive field pointed at a copy that did not list the asset; - keying by (archive, path) — still ambiguous inside an archive, for the reason above. Validated end-to-end through an independent code path (re-open the archive, fetch the blob by entry index , re-parse, confirm membership): 60/60 over ALL in bundle edges , up from 25/30 when lookups went t

t: LTAR v4 name resolution — CALIBRATED PER ARCHIVE (FIXED 2026-08-03)
x: The old resolve name offset took the string CONTAINING name offset plus a "if it lands on a NUL, step forward" special case. That made entries[i].path name the data at entries[i-1] — silently, since a neighbouring path still looks valid. Direction was settled by CONTENT, not shape: a BNDL manifest names its own assets, and name[i] matched the content of data[i-1] 40/40 while data[i+1] matched 0/40 ; no archive ever preferred +1. No single rule is right everywhere — LTAR v4 has packer VARIANTS. Over 3,161 content-verified entries in 65 archives, next wins 51 archives but every lighting archive prefers containing decisively (volcano lighting 27/30 vs next 0/30 ). The file variants (skip names-table strings with no extension, since folder paths are interleaved) dominate their plain counterparts everywhere and never lose. So the rule is calibrated per archive against content and cached in aire/data/engine/ltar name rules.json : rules chosen: next file 33, next 22, containing file 9, containing 1 confidence: 40 of 65 archives =0.95, 52 =0.80 Measured by the magic oracle (a .bndl -named entry must contain BNDL, scored where neighbours differ so alternating runs cannot fake agreement): 63

t: A NAME IS NOT AN ADDRESS — content-verified blob addressing (2026-08-03)
x: aire/formats/entry index.py ; call("entry index build") / call("asset blob", path=...) . The calibrated LTAR rule fixed the global naming error (63.8% - 95.2%) but every path-based extraction in AIRE still resolved a blob by NAME, and the residual is not spread evenly — it is concentrated exactly where the world data lives. Measured over all 479,031 entries in all 72 archives by reading each blob's true magic: 9,181 entries (1.9%) carry a name whose extension contradicts their content , and per archive that is ui assets 63.9%, corecharacter 35.1%, minasithil 35.0%, island 14.8%, volcano 14.0% . Consequence, measured: of 60 sampled worlds\ \sectionsandlayers\ .embb paths, 49 extracted to a blob that was not an EMBB at all — usually a neighbouring layer's small BNDL manifest, which then decodes to nothing and reads as "this layer is empty". t: PER-OBJECT TRANSFORMS CRACKED (2026-07-28) — `call("world_instances", path=...)`
x: The old ruling ("not unit quaternions — a full-file scan found zero") was an ALIGNMENT ARTIFACT , not a fact about the format. Instance records are packed at UNALIGNED byte offsets (a record's position field routinely starts at an address that is not a multiple of 4), so a 4-byte-aligned scan structurally could not see them. Read at every byte offset and the quaternions are there, unit-normalised. Never conclude "encoding X is absent" from an aligned scan of a packed format. Instance record — 0x32 (50) bytes, unaligned: Offset Type Field ------ ------- ------------------------------------------------------------------ +0x00 u16 link — 0xFFFF = root, else parent instance index +0x02 u32 name/string index (sequential 0,1,2… for a table's LEADING records only) +0x06 f32[3] position (world space) +0x12 f32[4] rotation quaternion (x,y,z,w), unit +0x22 u32 zero +0x26 u32 per-instance id +0x2A u32[2] monotone byte offsets into the name table Tables are located by the leading sequential-index signature (no wrong stride can fake a monotone 0,1,2,3 run), then extended by parse validity — requiring index==k throughout truncates a table early, because the index column is a name index, not a gl

t: PLACEMENT PROPERTIES CRACKED (2026-08-16) — OBJR holds an `ObjectPropertyDB`
x: The layer's OBJR section is not opaque geometry bookkeeping: it is a chunk registry whose GADB block is a full GADB v17 database named ObjectPropertyDB , and it carries what every placed object DOES. OBJR header 'OBJR' u32 ver(13) u32 hash u32 block count(14) blocks [u32 nameHash][u32 size][payload]; payload opens with a 4-char tag KEYF SFXS SWFX ONLS NLFE PFDG (unnamed) SCRB VOLM CAWR CADB GADB (unnamed) OBJL GADB block root type ObjectPropertyDB , category ObjectDB , records named ObjectRec Chain walks EXACTLY to EOF (60/60 layers chain exact , version 13 on all). Property DBs parse 120/120 layers, 0 failures, 21,814 rows ; 77 distinct Bip behaviours and 57 channels named across them. Parsing this at all requires the corrected desc start — see the string-block origin note below; ObjectPropertyDB is 17 characters and the old -16 window refused it. Row shapes (typed decode, values come out round and clean): spawner {spawner name, node ref, CHANNEL, NodeTag, removal policy, predicate} Trainer .MN Gondorian Soldier Orders Lead Stronghold Removal85M node/job {distances, NodeTag, Bip animation, node-set ref} Quest 0 10 10 Bip AbuseCaged Loop 10000 combat BattleAttacker Gondorian Soldie

t: WORLD-OBJECT LIVE LAYOUT (CRACKED 2026-08-03) — vptr +0x00, pos +0xAC, quat +0xB8
x: The 2026-08-03 ruling that "86% of coordinate hits have no owning vptr — placements live largely in plain buffers" is WITHDRAWN. It was an ALIGNMENT ARTIFACT — the same class of bug that once hid the on-disk instance table, recurring on the live side. derive from hits walked back from a coordinate hit in steps of 8 from the hit address . A coordinate is a float and 59% of hits land at 4 mod 8 (measured), so every qword the walk read straddled two real qwords and an intact vtable pointer could never appear. Stepping on machine-aligned addresses instead ( (hit & ~7) - 8k ) on the SAME hits: walk owners found --------------------------- ------------------- 8-step from the hit (old) 481 / 6,000 = 8.0% alignment-corrected 4,963 / 6,000 = 82.7% Reproduced across sessions (11.8% - 85.7%, then 8.0% - 82.7%). After two follow-up fixes — chunk-overlap in scan positions (a position triple straddling a 1 MB read boundary was dropped) and a single memoised owner walk shared by derive from hits + name vtables (two independent walks over a LIVE heap can return different owners for the same hit, so the class census could disagree with the offsets it was derived from) — steady state is 84-88% owner

t: Custom slots and `fm forcetrait` (BUILT, NOT RUN 2026-10-28)
x: A slot {picker, trait, +0x18 = 0, option} is never re-rolled: the resolver hands back its trait for every reason, and the reason-0 rebuild deactivates and re-activates it like every slot, so the engine's own activation gives everything the trait gives (items, gang cache, derived FM+0x508 bits, spawner hijack). It lasts until a save load: the loader re-adds the picker through 0x7CD03C , which copies the table flags back, and rolls it the game's way. A custom slot = flags 0 on a picker whose table flags are not 0. User request 2026-10-28 ("anything can be given ... minus the beast contradiction etc."). The Army Grid Traits menu has a Custom traits switch (on by default, session only). t: Orc Name Encoding (PROVEN 2026-04-15)
x: Game stores orc inline names (FM+0x498) in Latin-1 / Windows-1252 (single-byte encoding). Diacritics: û=0xFB, ê=0xEA, ô=0xF4, ú=0xFA. These are single bytes 0x7F. ImGui expects UTF-8. Must convert: Latin-1 byte b where b = 0x80 → two UTF-8 bytes (0xC0 (b 6)) + (0x80 (b & 0x3F)) . Do NOT pass raw high bytes through — ImGui renders them as ? . Do NOT break on byte 0x80 — it's a valid Latin-1 char; detect unused name slots by checking if ALL bytes are 0x80 (0x80-fill sentinel pattern).

t: GameDB Schema Format (PROVEN 2026-04-13)
x: Field Descriptor: 16 bytes each, stored in a contiguous array per schema. +0x00 u32 Field name hash (game-specific hash, P=919 polynomial) +0x04 u32 k-th entry of the run's ASCENDING sorted-hash list — a parallel array, NOT this descriptor's own sorted hash (CORRECTED 2026-07-28: Combat/Attack descriptor[0] is AnimationData yet carries ActionsOnAttackStart Source's hash). Run-boundary detection by monotone break is still valid — the list is what ascends. +0x08 u8 Absolute field index (inherited schema offset, may skip GROUP markers) MECHANISM (2026-10-05): a GROUP BEGIN/END marker IS a slot in the type's static schema object (PropRegister arg 7 = 0x80000080 / 0x40000080) but owns no field index, so index = slot - markers before it (Combat/Node: KBMNode slot 16 = index 14). See "GADB Field Bindings" +0x09 u8 Sort-order index +0x0A u8 TYPE CODE: 1=Boolean(4B), 2=Float(4B), 3=Integer(4B), 4=String(8B), 5=StringEnum(8B cell: P919 of an enum NAME), 6=Int64(8B), 7=Enum(4B: 32-bit POINTER to a shared (min,max) float-pool pair), 8=Vector3(12B), 9=Vector4(16B), 10=RecordLink(8B), 11=RecordLink to a PRIMARY record(8B), 68=String(8B) TYPE 5 IS A STRINGENUM, NOT A VECTOR2 (MEASURED 2026-10-19)

t: RecordLink On-Disk Encoding (CRACKED 2026-04-23)
x: Formula : RecordLink u32 = (category index 16) << 16 record index Equivalently: RL = (cat idx << 20) rec idx Decoding : cat idx = (RL 16) / 16 and rec idx = RL & 0xFFFF CRITICAL NOTES : 1. category index is the 0-based sequential index in the GADB's category array (sorted by hdr[5]) 2. record index is the 0-based index within the target category's record array 3. For categories with SECONDARY records (sc 0), rec idx indexes into secondary records 4. For Structures categories (inline struct arrays), rec idx indexes into PRIMARY records (pc) 5. 0xFFFFFFFF = null RecordLink (no reference) 6. 0x00000000 = null (record index 0 in category 0, treated as null in context) On-disk type 10 fields contain MIXED DATA — not all are true RecordLinks: - IEEE754 floats (e.g., 0x3F800000 =1.0, 0xBF800000 =-1.0) stored in type 10 slots - True RecordLinks have hi16 always a multiple of 16 (cat idx \ 16) - 65% of type 10 values are valid RecordLinks; 35% are float/int values Validation (2742 categories, 1,954,704 non-null type 10 values): - 1,271,632 values match formula (hi16 % 16 == 0, valid cat idx, valid rec idx) - 683,072 mismatches are ALL float values (0.8, 0.4, -1.0, etc.) - ZERO genuine Recor

t: GameDB Float-Range Pool (DISCOVERED 2026-04-14)
x: 148 Enum fields (type code 7) previously classified as "string ptr" are actually 32-bit pointers into a global float-pair parameter pool . Each pool entry = 8 bytes: (min, max) . These are shared templates — many records point to the SAME pool entry. Modifying one pool entry changes behavior for ALL records referencing it. Global tuning levers. Key moddable parameters: - AI/Perception.SimulatedRecognizeEnemyDistance : [1600, 2200] — detection range - AI/PursuitConstraint.Range : [500, 800] to [2500, 4500] — chase distances - AI/Alertness/TransitionPredicate.Duration : 0-10s — alert state timers - Combat/Hint/Distances.Distance : [0, 200] to [700, 2000] — combat distances - Combat/Predicates/Distance.Distance : [0, 40] to [200, 800] — trigger ranges ASLR : Pool pointers change every session. Live keys records by heap ADDRESS (dies with the process) or by NAME (ambiguous — see below); disk keys them by ORDINAL, RL = (cat idx 16) << 16 rec idx , which is unique and survives every restart. The Cell Identity Law proved the bijection in 2026-07; this materialises it, so a finding from session N re-points in session N+1 instead of being re-resolved by name with the ambiguity risk each time. - Alignment is MEASURED, never assumed : audit alignment() reads real record names on both sides. t: Primary Records — the other 60% of the GADB (CRACKED 2026-08-03)
x: The RecordLink spine originally addressed 278,865 secondary records = 40.1% of the database. The other 415,767 are PRIMARY records — the inline struct-array entries of 736 Structures categories. RecordLinks point at them, but nothing could resolve them. category +0x40 u32 primary count (400/400 categories == disk count) category +0x48 primary record array (stride 0x20, 250/250) primary +0x00 u32 field count primary +0x08 schema ptr primary +0x10 instance ptr (slot law holds: instances packed fc 8 apart) A primary header carries NO 0x0A tag byte. A secondary starts 06 0A 00 00 , a primary 06 00 00 00 . Every structural scan in the codebase keys on byte[1] == 0x0A , so primaries return ZERO hits and look like they do not exist. That single byte is why they were invisible. Validated 736/736 categories against the disk primary count, 0 mismatches ; decoded values are semantically coherent ( StructuresFactionDifficultyEntry primaries decode to the difficulty bands: [55,9999]- Enemy VeryHard , [30,55]- Enemy Hard , [10,30]- Enemy Easy ). Spine coverage is now 278,865 + 415,767 = 694,632 records = 100% of the GADB — a number that independently equals the engine graph's gamedb record entry

t: Record-Name Ambiguity (MEASURED 2026-07-28)

Worst: Default in 95 categories, Player 45, True 35, Balrog 35, Warg 25, Troll 25. An unscoped resolve record("Balrog") therefore returns a real, plausible-looking address that may belong to an entirely different category — silently. t: The `.fxp` load gate is ONE function, and it never sees a filename
x: LTFX occurs exactly once in the whole 120 MB binary , as an immediate in code: 0x048FBB90 FxResourceLoad(rcx, rdx = stream) mov rax,[rdx] ; mov r8d,8 ; lea rdx,[rsp+0x48] ; call [rax+8] <- stream- Read cmp dword [rsp+0x48], 'LTFX' / cmp dword [rsp+0x4C], 8 <- magic + version mov ecx,0x60 ; call 0x3DE238 ; call 0x74D000 <- new FxResource(0x60) call 0x74CF10 <- GADB-from-stream mov [rdi+0x48], rax <- db at FxResource+0x48 (fail) lea rcx,[0x20098E8] "Failed to load the database out of a stream." It is reached ONLY through vtable 0x2312340 slot 29 (39 slots, no RTTI; ctor 0x1D22C0C , dtor 0x1D22CC4 ) — a resource-type handler class, one virtual per asset kind. Path resolution happens UPSTREAM, so the loader takes a stream object whose vtable slot 1 is Read(dst,size) . That makes it a candidate in-process entry point for registering an effect with no file at all.

x: CGameClientShell::InitializeSubsystems 0x1772E1C creates five managers, one per time domain, with the strings "Could not init SimulationClientFXMgr!", "RealTime...", "PlayerTime...", "CompanionTime...", "WorldUIClientFXMgr". Factories 0x176DC70 (Simulation, arena 0x100000 = 1 MB) and 0x176DBF4 (the rest, arena 0x80000 = 512 KB): alloc 0x18358 - wrapper ctor 0x1779A64 - inner ctor 0x1779B20 ; init 0x177BB44(mgr, time source, flag) . Wrapper (vt 0x22F3178, 0x18358 B): +0x08 link {next, prev} in the global intrusive list headed at [base+0x26C6A98] ( 0x1BBC24 returns 0x26C6A90 ), +0x18 an embedded {vt 0x1DAA870, time source} pair, +0x28 the inner manager. vf1 0x482DE0 / vf2 0x482EB4 take a resource (its +0x20 id): the wrapper is a resource listener, so an effect resource that unloads kills its instances in every manager ( 0x482EC0 - 0x177C824 under the manager's lock). Live: 8 / 8 managers in the list, both vtables checked; a heap census found exactly 8 inner + 8 wrapper vtables (3.51 GB, untruncated). Inner ClientFXMgr (vt 0x1F67400, 32 small slots, 0x18330 B): +0x08 the ClientFXThreadMgr, +0x10 / +0x11 flags (+0x11 = threaded: queue work to the FX thread, else run it inline), +0x68..

t: Effect instances and how to enumerate them (MEASURED 2026-10-28, live)
x: Walk the manager's container, never the heap. inner+0xB8 is a std::vector of 0x28-byte entries; entry +0x18 is the instance. Two snapshots: 587 / 587 and 663 / 663 entries carried the instance vtable 0x1DAB360 . A heap census in the same session counted 927 objects with that vtable: the 340 extra are freed slots of the instance pool 0x2A3E9A8 that keep a stale vtable (BEHAVIOR.md law 7 again). The entry (0x28): +0x00 byte, +0x01 visible-this-frame, +0x02 budget-admitted, +0x04 cull position (3 floats, cm, world), +0x10 / +0x14 squared radii (a 40 m radius = 1.6e7 seen), +0x18 instance, +0x20 parent instance (child effects live in the PARENT's +0x18 vector, not in the manager's: 0x1BAD70 picks the container, stores it at instance +0x260 and the index at +0x25C). The FX instance (vt 0x1DAB360 + second vt 0x1DAB350 at +0x08; ctor 0x1BB368 , dtor 0x1BB79C "Failed to remove an effect correctly before destruction"): offset field --- --- +0x18 vector of child-effect entries (0x28 each) +0x40 intrusive list head (self-linked when empty) +0x58 flag word (bits 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 11, 13 set / cleared by ctor and init) +0x5C transform copied from the create struct (+0x38) +0xB8 the KeyData c

t: Budgets and caps (MEASURED 2026-10-28)
x: - Per manager: arena 1 MB (Simulation) / 512 KB; every frame the budget is reset to arena / 4 and each instance costs keys x 128 when first admitted, keys x 64 after; over budget - 0x177BFE8 . Live snapshot 2: Simulation 211,648 left of 262,144. Cvar ClientFXMgr.FXInstanceBudget (struct 0x266D4A0) feeds +0x19C / +0x1A0 from 0x266D4B8 / 0x266D4BC. - Per effect group (GameDB Client/ClientFXBudget , 7 records): MaxSimultaneousFX / MaxNewFX: OnFire 30 / 10, Blinded 25 / 10, BloodDecals 30 / 4, Poisoned 30 / 10, Footsteps 100 / 10, Easterling SmokeScreen 2 / 2, OnFire Balefire 30 / 10, plus FXList, BudgetExceededBehavior (EClientFXBudgetBehavior) and PoolingRules. LEAD: enforced at creation by the perf manager [GM+0x6DB8] ( 0x1BD23A check, 0x1BB5E0 register). - Distance: FxResource +0x04 MaxUpdateDistance; creation refused beyond the cull radius ( 0x1BB980 ); per-frame visibility from entry +0x10 / +0x14. - Particle caps are node properties (MaxParticleCapacity, MaxParticleLifeSpan, MaxParticleMethod, MaxParticleVelocity, SurfaceFireFXMaxParticlesFactor ), not a global pool.
